unit.why: Hagiographic account, copied from the preface of Tosefet Kedushah, of the ascetic habits of R. Yom Tov Lipman of Kapulye, a non-Hasidic rabbinic figure, with an anecdote showing his humility when a neighbour insulted his wife.

stories.start_quote: בהקדמת ס׳ תוספת קדושה (מהגה״ק יו״ט ליפמן
stories.summary_en: R. Yom Tov Lipman of Kapulye studied and sang Psalms day and night in the beit midrash and barely slept. When a neighbour insulted his wife and the communal leaders wanted to fine her, he forbade his wife to go to sleep before asking the neighbour's forgiveness; the neighbour wept and asked forgiveness in turn, and the town saw his humility.

tags.why: Praise of a non-Hasidic rabbi, copied from an earlier book's preface
Placed under the section on insults and forbearance as a lesson in humility and forgiveness
